name: Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA)
date_note: DORA already applies. Readiness is measured against an internal remediation target; set it to the date agreed with the board or supervisor.
articles_note: Article references are indicative; confirm against the supervisor's guidance.

requirements.summary: Maintain an ICT risk management framework covering identification, protection, detection, response and recovery, approved by the management body.

requirements.short: Classify and report major ICT incidents
requirements.summary: Classify ICT incidents and report major ones to the supervisor within the set deadlines.
Run a risk-based testing programme, including threat-led penetration testing where required.

requirements.short: Register of information and contract terms
requirements.summary: Keep a register of all ICT third-party arrangements and make sure contracts supporting critical functions carry the Article 30 terms, including exit plans.
ICT business continuity policy and response and recovery plans, tested regularly, with recovery time objectives for critical functions.

name: Solvency II review (Directive (EU) 2025/2)
status: Published in the Official Journal on 8 January 2025; applies at the latest from 30 January 2027.
date_note: Delegated regulation and technical standards set the detail; check the final texts.
articles_note: Summaries are EA paraphrase; confirm the applicable articles with compliance.

requirements.summary: Apply changes to the risk margin, risk-free rate extrapolation and long-term guarantee measures in capital calculations.

requirements.short: Climate and sustainability risk in the ORSA
requirements.summary: Assess material climate change risks in the ORSA, with long-term climate scenarios where material.
Liquidity risk management plans and macroprudential considerations in investment and risk management.
Adapt quantitative reporting templates and split the SFCR into a policyholder part and a market part.
Assess whether the insurer qualifies for proportionality measures and adapt processes if so.

name: EU Artificial Intelligence Act
status: In force since August 2024. Stand-alone high-risk obligations moved to 2 December 2027 under the 2026 provisional agreement (to confirm).
date_note: Dates follow the 2026 digital omnibus agreement; confirm the final adopted text.
articles_note: AI used for risk assessment and pricing in life and health insurance is listed as high-risk.

sources.title: Sidley: provisional agreement to delay key EU AI Act obligations

requirements.short: AI system inventory and risk classification
requirements.summary: Keep an inventory of AI systems and classify each by risk category.

requirements.short: Risk management and human oversight for high-risk AI
requirements.summary: For high-risk uses such as life and health pricing, run risk management, data governance, logging and human oversight.
Tell customers when they interact with an AI system such as a chatbot.
